Subject: Private offer request: multi-division term & approval routing

Jonas / Redwood team,

We're getting close to finalizing the platform decision for our telehealth division and two supporting internal teams. Procurement asked me to request a Marketplace private offer that will cover:
- 36 month term with annual invoicing
- Single subscription across three Acme AWS accounts (telehealth-prod, telehealth-staging, analytics)
- Upfront discount applied to committed spend, with the remainder billed monthly

Key asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood produce a private offer for a 36-month term and indicate what internal buyer approval thresholds apply for different discount levels?
2) We need to know the multi-account signoff process on the AWS Marketplace side — does AWS require each account owner to sign or can centralized procurement sign on behalf of the group?
3) Any special procurement paperwork (PO template, etc.) to attach to the private offer?

I'll attach a preliminary buyer list and PO template in follow-up. Looking to move quickly — target legal + procurement signoff by next Monday.

Thanks,
Susan Hopkins
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Health Systems
Attachments: none (will send buyer list & PO template)

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer request: multi-division term & approval routing

Susan — thanks for the clear ask. Happy to run this through Marketplace private offer flow. Quick answers up front:
- We can support a 36-month private offer and annual invoicing.
- Discount tiers we typically gate by buyer approval level (procurement only vs. executive sign-off) — I'll propose a matrix based on the expected ARR.
- For multi-account consolidation on AWS Marketplace, AWS needs to see the buyer authorizations; in many cases centralized procurement can sign if they have delegated authority across accounts. AWS marketplace sales can confirm the exact buyer signature requirements for Acme's org structure.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Can you send the buyer list (account owner emails) and a PO template — that will let us pre-fill the private offer and estimate approval routing time.
2) I'll loop in our Marketplace specialist (Vanessa Ortiz) and Legal (Karthik) to confirm signoff thresholds.

I can assemble a proposed approval matrix and three pricing scenarios (standard, committed discount, enterprise discount) by EOD Wednesday. Does that cadence work?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: none

Subject: FW: Private offer request: multi-division term & approval routing

Forwarding Acme's request — they want a 36-month offer across three accounts with annual invoicing. They want clarity on what buyer approvals are required for different discount levels and whether centralized procurement can sign for multiple accounts.

Proposed approach:
- Tier A (0-15% discount): procurement-only signoff (procurement@acmehealth.com)
- Tier B (16-30% discount): procurement + IT director approval (account owners)
- Tier C (>30% discount or >$250k ARR impact): procurement + CFO signoff (executive approval)

Vanessa — can you confirm AWS Marketplace multi-account signing behavior? If AWS requires per-account acceptance, we should flag increased lead time and offer a migration plan (centralized billing on our side via consolidated billing).
Karthik/Kimberly — legal and finance input on whether >30% / >$250k should trigger additional contract review or an exceptions process.

I'll draft the three pricing scenarios and include expected procurement windows per-tier.

--
Jonas
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Private offer request: multi-division term & approval routing

Jonas — quick legal/finance notes:
- Thresholds look reasonable. Add a clause that any renewal beyond year 1 may be subject to repricing if usage materially exceeds forecasts (protects both sides).
- For Tier C approvals (>30% or >$250k): require documented executive email signoff + procurement PO. We should also route the private offer with a comment that legal review was completed to avoid re-openings.
- Multi-account: AWS Marketplace supports buyer delegation but requires evidence of delegated authority (procurement letter or equivalent). We should provide a short template procurement delegation letter Acme can use.

I can draft the delegation letter template and the executive signoff checklist. Vanessa — if AWS requires individual account acceptance, estimate the additional time and whether the acceptance can be batched.

Karthik

Susan — received, thanks. Summary of next steps and deliverables from Redwood:  
1) Pricing scenarios (standard / committed / enterprise) and approval matrix (today by EOD Monday) — I'll attach draft PO and populate with Acme details.
2) Delegation letter template and executive signoff checklist (Karthik is drafting).
3) Marketplace mechanics: Vanessa confirmed that AWS Marketplace accepts delegated procurement letters; for multi-account acceptance, AWS prefers either (a) centralized procurement acceptance with delegation letter, or (b) per-account acceptance. Centralized acceptance with delegation typically reduces lead time. Vanessa will open an internal AWS ticket to confirm the co-sell registration requirements and expected approval SLA (we'll include the ticket id in the private offer comment).
4) DocuSign & PO: we'll prepare a DocuSign PO pre-filled and the private offer draft. Expect a DocuSign link by Monday; once signed, Redwood will submit the private offer to AWS and include the delegation letter.
